summary: The exact candidate commit 8c342b1aea310267115f223bfbb9573791147543 upgrades xgrammar from 0.2.1 to 0.2.2 and adds a focused regression. With the real 0.2.2 compiler/native binding, it rejects the issue's invalid named object while accepting the named integer and a valid additional field. However, it still rejects a valid object when the additional field precedes the named field. Because JSON object member order is semantically irrelevant, the candidate only partially restores properties + schema-valued additionalProperties semantics and its regression does not cover this remaining contract failure.

tests.what_was_measured: Reproduced the original named-property dilution through SGLang's actual structural-tag builder and xgrammar compiler: invalid data-as-object was accepted. Also established ordering behavior on the prepared base.

The candidate's focused regression passed against exact candidate source and the xgrammar 0.2.2 native wheel: valid named integer accepted, invalid named object rejected, and one valid unknown property accepted.
Independent contract cases against the real compiler. Nine cases behaved as expected, but a valid object with the additional property before the named property was rejected.
Candidate Kimi-K3 structural-tag unit file: 36 passed. This suite does not cover the remaining order-dependent valid case.

gpu_execution.evidence: The original issue and all relevant validation are deterministic CPU-only grammar compilation/matching; no model inference or GPU kernel is involved.

remaining_counterexamples: For schema {properties: {data: integer}, additionalProperties: object-with-required-string-data}, the valid JSON value {"extra":{"data":"ok"},"data":2} is rejected by the xgrammar 0.2.2 grammar, while the semantically equivalent member order {"data":2,"extra":{"data":"ok"}} is accepted.
remaining_limitations: No Kimi-K3 weights or server deployment were exercised; the issue's authoritative deterministic path is the actual SGLang structural-tag builder plus xgrammar compiler.
Candidate source changes are Python manifests and tests only. No SGLang or FlyDSL native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.

xgrammar 0.2.2 was validated from its released CPython 3.12 x86_64 manylinux wheel and native library at /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-68ab44ca5334/xgrammar-0.2.2/xgrammar/libxgrammar_bindings.so. Other architectures were not tested.
The prepared host is x86_64 with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2.26015, but GPU execution is unrelated to this CPU-only grammar defect.
